notes: 142 claims were read. Most are internal to the archive (self-referential tests, Space Ark transforms, future fictional citations, capture batteries on the archive's own entities) and have no outside test; outside evidence was sought for about twenty that name a measurable effect or a general mechanism. Every witness recorded here bears as mechanism, method or component; none bears on a claim as a whole, because the claims concern the archive's own deposits and the outside research does not. Most witnesses predate their claims and will order as anticipations; those after registration are E-execution-W02 (2026-10-02, after PRED-139.F1 2026-05-29), W09 and W10 (2026-05-13, after PRED-42.B1 2026-03-26), W20 (2026-04-06, after PRED-218.F1 and PRED-219.F1, 2026-01-03). W03 (2026-05-17), W23 (2026-05-25) and W28 (2026-05-11) fall weeks before their claims and are anticipations. The order script computes this; the reader's reckoning is only a guide. PRED-194.A1 falsifier (c): checked 2026-10-30, the official OWASP LLM Top 10 is still the 2025 edition and no NIST AI 100-2 edition after E2025 was found, so the falsifier has not fired; window runs to 2028-06-12. The NIST E2025 definitions of prompt injection could not be read through the fetch tool (sections 3.3, 3.4 and the glossary fell outside the returned text); a reader with the PDF should quote them before any NIST witness is recorded. Three sources are recorded twice in opposite directions on different components: Souly et al. (W05 supports, W06 disconfirms the corpus-share term of PRED-127.B1), Negation Neglect (W09 supports for the training layer, W10 disconfirms for the in-context stage of PRED-42.B1), FABLES (W15 supports method, W16 disconfirms the 'current benchmarks do not test' component of PRED-34.F2). The main session may prefer to merge them. PRED-176.F1 has a split record: GEO (W21) supports that presentation changes visibility; Wan et al. (W22) and Vishwakarma et al. (W23) find relevance dominates and stylistic or formatting cues matter little. Meeus et al. 2024 (W07) is already cited inside the archive at PRED-1384.F4. The fetch tool caps quotes at about 125 characters, so findings are short fragments; each was returned by the tool as verbatim from the page named. The GEO quote keeps the LaTeX '$40\%$' as the arXiv abstract served it. Peer-reviewed venues known only from search results (ICML, ICLR, USENIX, NeurIPS, ACL, KDD, Findings of EMNLP, COLM) are named in source.venue and listed in checked.unverified; the evidence_class of those witnesses is set to preprint, the version actually read. The main session may raise a class after confirming the venue page.
